core_obligations: Assume PT for fields and let R -> Lambda be a counterexample; the set of ideals I with R/I -> Lambda/ILambda failing PT has a maximal element by Noetherianity; after replacing, PT holds modulo every nonzero ideal.
The proposition-lift assembly then shows R is reduced (else a nonnilpotent square-zero extension would violate maximality).

Let Q = S^{-1}R be the total ring of fractions, a product of fields K_1 x ... x K_n; PT holds for S^{-1}R -> S^{-1}Lambda by the product lemma and the field hypothesis, giving a factorization S^{-1}A -> B' -> S^{-1}Lambda with B' smooth.
Apply delocalize-base: get a factorization A -> B -> Lambda with some pi in S elementary standard in B over R; replace A by B so pi is strictly standard in A over R.

PT modulo pi^8 gives a smooth R/pi^8R-algebra bar-C factoring A/pi^8A -> Lambda/pi^8Lambda; the lifting lemma produces D -> Lambda smooth over R with a mod-pi^4 factorization through bar-C; the desingularize-strictly-standard lemma converts this into a factorization A -> B'' -> Lambda with B'' smooth over R, contradicting the choice of I.
proof_roadmap: Noetherian induction on bad ideals; reducedness via the deformation proposition; total fraction ring product of fields; elementary standard denominator; lifting and desingularization finish.
difficulty_reason: A five-step reduction argument; each step goes through a named input and the final two are the chapter's lifting pair, all carried.
